topic.title: HTML — Quick Revision
topic.subtitle: Semantics, forms, accessibility and SEO in one sitting.

questions.q: What is semantic HTML and why does it matter?

answer.value: Semantic elements describe the meaning of content (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `article`, `section`, `aside`, `footer`) instead of using generic `div`s. Benefits: accessibility (screen readers can navigate landmarks), SEO, and more readable code.

questions.q: Difference between block, inline and inline-block elements?

items: **Block** (`div`, `p`) starts on a new line and takes full width.
**Inline** (`span`, `a`) flows within text; width/height and vertical margins don't apply.
**Inline-block** flows inline but accepts width, height and margins.

answer.value: `<!DOCTYPE html>` tells the browser to render in standards mode. Without it browsers fall back to quirks mode with legacy layout behaviour.

items: Plain `<script>`: blocks HTML parsing while it downloads and runs.
`async`: downloads in parallel, runs as soon as ready (order not guaranteed).
`defer`: downloads in parallel, runs after parsing finishes, in order.

answer.value: Use `defer` for scripts that depend on the DOM or on each other; `async` for independent scripts like analytics.

questions.q: How do you make a page accessible?

items: Use semantic elements and a logical heading order.
Give every image meaningful `alt` text (empty `alt=""` for decorative ones).
Associate every input with a `<label>`.
Make everything keyboard reachable with a visible focus style.
Use ARIA only when native HTML can't express the role; keep colour contrast sufficient.

questions.q: What is the difference between <div> and <span>?

answer.value: `div` is a block-level generic container for layout; `span` is an inline generic container for styling part of text. Neither carries meaning.

questions.q: How do HTML forms work? Name common input types and validation attributes.

answer.value: A `<form>` groups controls and submits their `name`/value pairs to its `action` using `method` GET or POST. Input types include `text, email, password, number, date, checkbox, radio, file, range, tel, url`. Built-in validation: `required, min, max, minlength, maxlength, pattern, type`.

items: **localStorage**: ~5 MB, persists until cleared, never sent to the server.
**sessionStorage**: same API, cleared when the tab closes.
**Cookies**: ~4 KB, sent with every request, can expire and be `HttpOnly`/`Secure`.

questions.q: What are meta tags? Which ones matter most?

items: `<meta charset="utf-8">` — character encoding.
`<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` — responsive layout on mobile.
`description`, Open Graph (`og:title`, `og:image`) — search and social previews.

questions.q: How do responsive images work (srcset, sizes, picture)?

answer.value: `srcset` + `sizes` let the browser pick the best file for the screen width and pixel density; `<picture>` with `<source>` swaps formats or art direction. Add `loading="lazy"` for below-the-fold images and always set width/height to avoid layout shift.
`strong` and `em` convey importance/emphasis (screen readers may change tone); `b` and `i` are purely stylistic.

questions.q: What is the difference between id and class?

answer.value: `id` must be unique per page and identifies one element (anchors, labels, JS hooks). `class` can be reused on many elements and combined. In CSS, id selectors have higher specificity.

items: `<dialog>`: native modal/non-modal dialog (`showModal()`).
`<details>`/`<summary>`: built-in disclosure widget.
`<template>`: inert markup you clone with JS.

questions.q: What happens when you type a URL and press Enter?

items: DNS lookup resolves the domain to an IP.
TCP (and TLS) connection is established.
Browser sends the HTTP request; server responds with HTML.
The browser parses HTML into the DOM and CSS into the CSSOM, builds the render tree.
Layout, paint and composite; scripts and other resources load along the way.
